data.title: I'm terrified of a market crash. Should I put $400,000 of my $1 million retirement savings into an annuity?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'We have a house worth $450,000. Our combined annual income is $125,000.'

"We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Quentin,

I'm wondering what your thoughts are on putting our house and other assets into a trust. Could it help reduce taxes or protect our assets from lawsuits, bankruptcy or other unforeseen circumstances? If so, what are the potential downsides or pitfalls?

We have a house worth $450,000 and about $1 million in retirement assets held in various qualified accounts. I'd also be interested in your thoughts on annuities for capital preservation and guaranteed income.

Would it make sense to put $400,000 of our $1 million in qualified retirement accounts into an annuity that would begin paying out at age 65, guaranteeing us $40,000 a year for life, while leaving the remaining $600,000 invested in a brokerage account for capital appreciation?

My spouse and I are 55 and 54, respectively. We're both working and plan to continue until 65. We're terrified of a market crash. We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000.

Curious in the Midwest

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'Nvidia has me spooked ': Should I sell my stocks or buy real estate?

That money you invest in an annuity is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Dear Curious,

I'll outline the advantages of your proposal - and then move on to the cons.

First, the pros of putting your money in an annuity, I presume, are to find a haven for part of your nest egg, albeit at a potentially lower rate than the stock market could provide. If you moved $400,000 from traditional 401(k)s or IRAs into an IRA annuity, the transaction generally would not trigger income taxes or the 10% early-withdrawal penalty, provided the funds are transferred correctly. A direct trustee-to-trustee transfer is typically the simplest approach. If you were selling $400,000 worth of investments in an ordinary brokerage account, however, you could owe capital-gains taxes on any profits realized from the sale.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security, which you presumably plan to take when you reach full retirement age. What you receive depends on the type of annuity: your initial investment, the interest rate or other terms you lock in and, of course, the payment schedule. Payouts can also vary with your age, your sex and whether the product is a joint-life annuity. If you expect to live a long time, a lifetime annuity can protect you from outliving your retirement savings. The trade-off is access: That money is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security.

An annuity is neither a bond nor cash. It works as an insurance contract: you pay an insurance company in exchange for income. An immediate annuity starts paying within a year of purchase, while a deferred annuity starts at a later date. Money in a 401(k) or IRA that is invested in stocks can grow over time and help keep pace with inflation. Annuity income is usually fixed, so it can lose purchasing power as prices rise unless you add an inflation adjustment or rider, but that protection also comes at a price: a lower initial payout. Annuity fees can be as much as 10% of the value of your contract. Surrender charges can be substantial if you withdraw money early.

But I have some questions: I understand why the prospect of $40,000 in guaranteed annual income is tempting. If payments continued for those periods, you would collect $400,000 over 10 years, $800,000 over 20 years and potentially $1.2 million over 30 years. Make sure you read the fine print. Is that $40,000 guaranteed income for one person's lifetime? Or is it for both of your lifetimes? Does the surviving spouse continue to receive the full $40,000-a-year income? Is there a death benefit or return-of-premium provision or rider if one spouse dies? Last but not least, are the $40,000-a-year payments adjusted for inflation?

Don't miss: My wife and I are in our 70s. Should we pay off our 2.5% mortgage or invest in a stock market driven by AI?

Investing in the stock market

Third, the pros of leaving the money in the stock market: If you left your $400,000 invested for another 10 years instead of putting it into an annuity, it could grow to approximately $592,000 at an annual return of 4%, $787,000 at 7%, or $864,000 at 8%. These estimates assume annual compounding, with investment earnings reinvested, and exclude taxes, fees and additional contributions. The biggest difference between this scenario and the option of buying an annuity with your $400,000 is that the former is not guaranteed. You are potentially giving up the prospect of a larger return in exchange for security.

An annuity and a trust provide different estate-planning functions. Annuities distribute your assets per the terms of the contract, whereas a trust is designed to manage, protect and distribute your estate during your lifetime and beyond. As this guide on Estate Guru points out, trusts and annuities solve different estate-planning problems: (1) Bypassing probate or buying an annuity isn't an estate plan. (2) A trust can manage your assets if you become incapacitated, provide for minor children or beneficiaries with special needs, address the complications of a blended family and set out the conditions for an inheritance.

Revocable living trusts can benefit people with modest estates, particularly those seeking to avoid probate or plan for incapacity. For families with complicated estates, putting accounts and assets under a single trustee can keep everything running smoothly. It can also help prevent conflicts involving beneficiary designations. Marital trusts matter most in blended families, where each spouse wants to be sure their own children are provided for if the other dies. A special-needs trust can supplement government benefits, while a spendthrift trust can prevent beneficiaries from selling or using their future inheritance as collateral for a loan.

Know what you're buying, and be sure you're doing it for the right reasons.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.

data.title: Marrelli Capital Limited and Salma and Noah Limited Partnership - Joint Early Warning News Release Regarding Common Shares of Longview Capital (No. 1) Inc.
data.description:
TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / Marrelli Capital Limited ("MCL"), an Ontario Corporation, and Salma and Noah Limited Partnership ("SNLP"),an Ontario limited partnership, announce that they have each filed an early warning report (each an "EWR" and collectively, the "EWRs") in respect of common shares ("Shares") of Longview Capital (No. 1) Inc. (formerly BE Resources Inc.) (the "Company").

On November 24, 2026, MCL sold an aggregate of 2,536,392 Shares, representing approximately 22.33% of the 11,357,940 issued and outstanding Shares, to SNLP for total consideration of C$19,998.00 (approximately C$0.0079 per Share) (the "Transaction"). The Transaction was a transfer between affiliated entities under common control. It was completed by private agreement and did not take place on any market. SNLP relied on the private agreement exemption in section 4.2 of National Instrument 62-104 Take-Over Bids and Issuer Bids. The Shares were purchased from one seller, MCL, by private agreement; the purchase was not made to securityholders of the Company generally; and there is no published market for the Shares.

Immediately prior to the Transaction, MCL held 2,536,392 Shares, representing approximately 22.33% of the issued and outstanding Shares, and SNLP held nil Shares. Immediately following the Transaction, SNLP holds 2,536,392 Shares, representing approximately 22.33% of the issued and outstanding Shares, and MCL holds nil Shares. MCL previously filed an early warning report dated July 6, 2026 in respect of the Shares, which MCL's EWR updates to reflect the Transaction.

SNLP acquired the Shares from MCL for investment purposes and as part of a reorganization of shareholdings among entities under common control. MCL, SNLP and their joint actors are aware that the Company has called an annual and special meeting of shareholders for December 18, 2026 to consider, among other things, the continuance of the Company from Ontario into British Columbia and the adoption of new articles, that the Company intends to relocate its head office to Vancouver, British Columbia following the continuance, and that its board of directors is evaluating a potential reorganization by way of a plan of arrangement under which shares of one or more newly incorporated subsidiaries of the Company would be distributed to shareholders, each as described in the Company's management information circular dated November 9, 2026. No agreement has been entered into in respect of the potential reorganization, its terms have not been settled, and there is no assurance that it will be proposed or completed.

Other than as described above, MCL, SNLP and their joint actors have no current plans or future intentions that relate to or would result in any of the matters described in Item 5 of Form 62-103F1. Depending on the Company's business and prospects and other factors, MCL, SNLP and their joint actors may in the future acquire additional securities of the Company, or dispose of some or all of the securities of the Company that they hold, by private agreement or otherwise, subject in each case to applicable securities laws.

The head office of the Company and the address of each of MCL and SNLP is located at 82 Richmond Street East, Toronto, Ontario M5C 1P1. Copies of the EWRs are available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and may also be obtained by contacting Marie-Josee Audet by email at maudet@marrellisupport.ca or by telephone at (416) 278-5519.

Forward-Looking Information
This news release contains forward-looking information, including statements about the intentions of MCL, SNLP and their joint actors with respect to securities of the Company, and about the Company's proposed continuance, head office relocation and potential reorganization as described in its management information circular dated November 9, 2026. These statements reflect the current intentions of MCL and SNLP and the Company's public disclosure as of the date of this news release. They are subject to risks, including that the continuance may be delayed or abandoned, that required shareholder, regulatory and court approvals may not be obtained, that the potential reorganization may not be proposed or completed on any terms, and that the intentions of MCL, SNLP and their joint actors may change with market conditions and other factors. Readers should not place undue reliance on forward-looking information. MCL and SNLP undertake no obligation to update it except as required by applicable securities laws.

SOURCE: Salma and Noah Limited Partnership.

data.title: I hate that Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia, but I love what it's done for my 401(k). Am I a hypocrite?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods

Jensen Huang, who on Monday returned as CEO of Nvidia. (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I was paralyzed during the market downturn, so I have a question in the event that this bounce - led by the shocking and, in my opinion, unwelcome news that Jensen Huang has returned as Nvidia's (NVDA) CEO - does not last. No comment on that, as it happens, even though I have my opinions, like most people do.

I'm writing to you about my own strategy, not to pass judgment on other people's corporate decisions. During a market downturn, is it better for me to draw down cash from CDs for the next year or two rather than taking money from my equities and annuities at a loss? Where are the safe havens? I don't want to eat into my retirement savings.

Planning Ahead

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: America is divided into two countries - Trump's pro-billionaires and Mamdani's anti-billionaires

Being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing.

Dear Planning,

It's fair to say that many people were surprised by Jensen Huang's return on Monday - and you are not alone in having strong opinions on that.

Some of the same people who cried foul over the fall in their 401(k)s and IRAs may well be rolling their eyes over the return of Huang to the helm of Nvidia, which now appears to be the cornerstone of the AI revolution, mostly due to its multibillion-dollar microchip business and proprietary software ecosystem. Indeed, the stock gave up some of Monday's gains on Tuesday as investors turned their attention to regulatory concerns about the export of U.S. microchips to China and elsewhere. Huang was effectively fired (he officially resigned) from the company a couple of weeks ago over his reported affairs with two employees, as well as one with a woman who has been accused of being a Chinese spy.

Commentators have questioned whether President Donald Trump overlooked the potential and alleged national-security threat by calling for Huang's return to Nvidia NVDA, thereby signaling that the company is too big to fail. Others bemoaned the decision by the company's board and wondered what the role of such boards is, if not to uphold professional, legal and personal standards. While low-wage American workers have been fired over bathroom breaks, skeptics may wonder if rules of conduct only apply to nonbillionaires.

It's OK to have joys and concerns about the billionaire class and your 401(k), even if the answers conflict with each other.

And, honestly, being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing, either. Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods. Some people panic and sell, or move into real estate, bonds, or gold, and constantly check their 401(k) while getting upset over paper losses. Yet short-term swings won't have a big impact if they aren't about to retire or haven't just retired - especially if they have cash alternatives. How many times a day or week did you check your 401(k) when the market was on the rise? I'm guessing not a lot.

I sympathize with your urge to check. According to a 2026 report by the Investment Company Institute (ICI), a global trade association representing regulated funds and their shareholders, 81% of mutual fund-owning U.S. households hold stock funds - most of them inside workplace retirement plans. Because broad stock and index funds are heavily weighted toward mega-cap AI leaders like Nvidia, a significant share of American households are naturally exposed to those stocks. "Mutual funds play a key role in their households' balance sheets," the researchers wrote.

But back to the other questions in your letter: Yes, drawing from CDs and relying on annuity income can be a smart move. That assumes you don't have required minimum distributions from a traditional retirement account and your CDs have reached the end of their term. If you paid extra for a guaranteed lifetime income rider on your annuities - locking in an income stream if markets plummet or your account balance falls to zero - that will protect you during a correction, while fixed annuities aren't tied to the market's fortunes at all. Having cash alternatives helps you avoid "sequence-of-returns risk," where poor market performance in the early years of retirement puts pressure on a portfolio you're drawing from.

Don't miss: 'Nvidia's turmoil has me spooked': Is it time to sell my stocks and buy real estate?

Timing the market vs. managing risk

Darius Dale, founder and CEO of 42 Macro, a macroeconomic research and systematic risk-management firm, predicts that markets will return to a "risk-on market regime," where investors favor higher risk assets over safe havens, within a couple of months. "Hope is not an effective risk-management process," he says. "Positioning for the market regime helps investors avoid fear of missing out (FOMO) and fear of more losses (FOML). FOMO causes investors to buy cycle tops, and FOML causes investors to sell cycle lows. These are the two worst things any investor can do to their financial well-being."

As for your curiosity about safe havens, I can understand why you would consider them after such a volatile week, especially with lingering questions about the stock market's heavy dependence on AI. The right mix depends on your risk tolerance and, as Dale suggested, your expectations about the economic outlook, especially if you want to factor in how reliant the economy is becoming on AI. There are many paths to take. Andrew Clinton, CEO of Clinton Investment Management, suggests municipal bonds as a haven during a correction.

I can understand why you would look for safe havens, especially with lingering questions about the market's heavy dependence on AI.

Municipal bonds are, for the record, more appropriate for investors in higher tax brackets with money held in taxable accounts who live in high-tax states, and for retirees prioritizing cash flow and capital preservation. "Municipal bonds offer attractive tax-adjusted carry and stable underlying asset-class credit quality for investors seeking durable cash flows amidst equity-market volatility," he says. "Current municipal bond yields remain near the most attractive levels in decades."

Clinton also has a rosier outlook on the underlying strength of the U.S. economy than, perhaps, many folks. "Credit fundamentals remain strong, with default rates representing only a fraction of corporate default rates," he says. "Municipal issuers provide essential services such as airports, utilities and toll roads, generating durable cash flows with limited exposure to corporate earnings volatility. If inflation moderates and rates decline, municipals offer the potential for both attractive income and capital appreciation."

For other safe havens, consider shorter-duration bonds, mutual funds and exchange-traded funds that invest in bonds with maturities of less than five years, as well as Treasury inflation-protected securities (TIPS) backed by the U.S. Treasury to guard against rising prices. Give a thought to value-oriented and defensive sectors, including consumer-staples, utilities and healthcare stocks, for retired investors who seek stability over higher returns. Your lifestyle, the balances in your retirement accounts, your goals, your financial profile - whether you have a mortgage, debt or long-term-care insurance - and your views on AI all play a role.

Pausing during a storm does not mean you suffer from paralysis, and you don't have to like the news in order to plan around it.

Your letter attests to that.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.

data.title: TC Energy announces second Indigenous investment in Coastal GasLink
data.description:
CALGARY, Alberta, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TC Energy Corporation (TSX, NYSE: TRP) (TC Energy or the Company) today announced the closing of an agreement with CGL First Nations Limited Partnership (CGL FNLP), an Indigenous-led investment entity representing 12 First Nations along the Coastal GasLink (CGL) corridor, including Cheslatta Carrier Nation; Kitselas First Nation; Lheidli T’enneh First Nation; Nadleh Whut’en First Nation, Nee Tahi Buhn Indian Band; Saik’uz First Nation; Skin Tyee Nation; Stellat'en First Nation; Ts’il Kaz Koh First Nation; Wet’suwet’en First Nation; Witset First Nation; and Yekooche First Nation.

Through the agreement, participating Nations have acquired an economic interest in the entity that holds TC Energy’s limited partner interest in CGL. These communities are expected to benefit from long-term predictable financial returns associated with TC Energy’s limited partner interest in CGL.

This transaction marks the second Indigenous investment involving TC Energy's interest in CGL and reflects years of partnership with Indigenous communities along the corridor.

Creating opportunities through partnership
“This transaction demonstrates what is possible when Indigenous communities, industry and governments come together with a shared commitment to creating opportunities that deliver benefits over the long term,” said François Poirier, President and Chief Executive Officer of TC Energy. “It reflects the strength of the relationships developed along the Coastal GasLink corridor over more than a decade of collaboration and our shared belief that major projects should create lasting value for the communities connected to them.”

“This investment represents a historic milestone for our Nations and a new chapter in our relationship with Coastal GasLink,” said Corrina Leween, Director & Executive Committee member, CGL FNLP. “It reflects years of work to advance Indigenous participation in major infrastructure projects and to create a stronger role for our Nations in shaping the economic future of our territories. Through this transaction, our Nations will benefit from a long-term economic interest that provides stable, predictable returns for our communities, helping support future generations and strengthen our collective prosperity. Today’s achievement would not have been possible without the vision and leadership of the late Niilo Edwards, whose commitment to Indigenous economic empowerment helped bring our Nations together around this opportunity.”

Expanding pathways to participation
This transaction was supported by a loan guarantee made available under the Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Program, administered by the Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Corporation (CILGC).

“We commend TC Energy for working with CGL First Nations Limited Partnership to advance this investment. Partnerships like this can support a more inclusive approach to infrastructure development while strengthening Indigenous economic self-determination and creating opportunities for Nations to share in long-term, project benefits,” said Kristan Straub, President and CEO, Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Corporation.

“At a time when Canada must build big things again, in partnership with Indigenous Peoples, projects like Coastal GasLink are helping us strengthen our economic sovereignty, diversify our trade, advance reconciliation and Indigenous prosperity, and secure our place as a global energy superpower. By combining Indigenous economic participation with the investment certainty needed to advance major projects, we are responsibly driving Canada's next generation of growth,” said the Honourable Tim Hodgson, Minister of Energy and Natural Resources.

“Economic reconciliation is about ensuring that Indigenous communities have the opportunity to own, invest in, and benefit from the major projects shaping Canada’s future. This investment will support 12 First Nations in acquiring an interest in, and derive meaningful long-term benefits from, one of Canada’s most important energy infrastructure projects. By helping unlock Indigenous ownership in major projects, we are creating opportunities to build long-term wealth, generate sustainable revenues, and advance economic self-determination for generations to come,” said the Honourable François-Philippe Champagne, Minister of Finance and National Revenue.

Building on more than a decade of partnership
For many participating Nations, this agreement represents the next chapter in a relationship with CGL that spans more than a decade.

The investment opportunity was made available to all 20 Indigenous communities with existing CGL agreements. Participation reflects the independent decisions of each Nation based on its own priorities and objectives.

On Oct. 13, 2026, TC Energy announced its first Indigenous investment agreement related to CGL, involving participating Nations represented through FN CGL Pipeline Limited Partnership. Together, the two agreements build on years of partnership and create additional opportunities for Indigenous communities to benefit from the long-term financial returns associated with TC Energy's limited partner interest in CGL.

A critical pathway for Canadian LNG exports
As operator and co-owner of CGL, TC Energy safely delivers 2.1 billion cubic feet per day of Canadian natural gas to LNG Canada in Kitimat, B.C., supporting Canadian LNG exports to global markets. With the announcement of CGL Phase 2, system capacity will nearly double, demonstrating the growing global demand for natural gas and long-term value of Canadian LNG exports.

Transaction advisors
RBC Capital Markets acted as financial advisor to TC Energy and Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP as legal counsel.

For CGL First Nations Limited Partnership, National Bank of Canada Capital Markets acted as business and financial advisors, and Gowling WLG acted as legal counsel.

About TC Energy
We are a leader in North American energy infrastructure, spanning Canada, the U.S. and Mexico. For over 75 years, we have proudly connected the world to the energy it needs. Every day, we move more than 30 per cent of the natural gas used across the continent and connect LNG exports to global markets—powering communities and industries. Complemented by strategic ownership and low-risk investments in power generation, our infrastructure delivers affordable, reliable and sustainable energy across North America. 

We carry forward a legacy of nation building energy infrastructure and strong partnerships. By working with communities, businesses and leaders across our extensive energy network, we create opportunities today and for generations to come. 

TC Energy’s common shares trade on the Toronto (TSX) and New York (NYSE) stock exchanges under the symbol TRP. To learn more, visit us at TCEnergy.com.

About Coastal GasLink
CGL is Canada’s first direct pathway to global LNG export markets. It is a 670-kilometre (416-mile) natural gas pipeline that safely delivers 2.1 Bcf/d of natural gas from northeastern British Columbia to the LNG Canada facility in Kitimat, B.C., where it is liquefied for export to global markets. The infrastructure is owned by Coastal GasLink Pipeline Limited Partnership, with TC Energy as the operator.

About CGL First Nations Limited Partnership
CGL First Nations Limited Partnership comprises of 12 First Nations that will collectively hold an economic interest in the entity holding TC Energy’s limited partner interest in the Coastal GasLink project. The partnership was established to pursue collective economic opportunities and advance Indigenous ownership in the Coastal GasLink project, creating long-term benefits for participating Nations and future generations.

Forward-looking statements in this release include, without limitation, statements regarding: the expected benefits of the transaction to participating Nations, including long-term, predictable financial returns associated with TC Energy’s limited partner interest in CGL; anticipated increase in pipeline transportation capacity with Phase 2, and expectations regarding global demand for natural gas and the long-term value of Canadian LNG exports.

data.title: Organto Foods Delivers Record Third Quarter 2026 Results
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC AND BREDA, THE NETHERLANDS / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / Organto Foods Inc. (TSXV:OGO)(OTCQX:OGOFF)(FSE:OGF0) ("Organto" or "the Company"), is pleased to announce its financial results for the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026. All amounts are expressed in Canadian dollars and in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), except where specifically noted.

"Q-3 2026 was another record quarter for our Company. Our third quarter sales grew 67% to $25.2 million, the largest third quarter sales in the history of the Company, while gross profit, adjusted gross profit (1) and adjusted EBITDA (1) also reached third quarter records. Equally important, our balance sheet remains strong with $14.5 million of working capital, no long-term debt and net equity of $15.6 million. Following our business repositioning through 2024 and early 2025, our goal was to continue to expand our commercial and operating base, while positioning to achieve positive adjusted EBITDA (1) in 2026. We have realized these objectives and in fact this quarter represents our third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA (1) results, demonstrating the strength and adaptability of our scalable, capital-efficient ecosystem. These results reinforce our confidence in the opportunities that lie ahead as we continue to build a world-class organic and fairtrade foods company." commented Steve Bromley, Co-Chair and Chief Executive Officer.

Key Highlights

  • Sales increased 67% to a third quarter record of $25.2 million. Largest third quarter sales in Company's history.
  • Adjusted gross profit (1) when accounting for the impact of currency hedging related to gross profit increased to $2.1 million or 8.2% of sales, an increase of 206% versus the prior year. Largest third quarter gross profit and adjusted gross profit (1) dollars in the Company's history.
  • Cash overhead expenses (1) decreased to 7.8% of sales versus 8.9% in the prior year, demonstrating continued operating leverage.
  • Adjusted EBITDA (1) improved to $0.3 million from a loss of $0.7 million in the prior year. Largest third quarter adjusted EBITDA (1) in the Company's history.
  • Annualized sales run rate (2) continues in excess of $100 million.
  • Working capital increased to $14.5 million.
  • No long-term debt outstanding.
  • Cash balance remained strong at $7.9 million.
  • Equity of $15.6 million, up 78% versus December 31, 2025

Steve Bromley further commented, "We remain focused and committed to building a world-class organic and fairtrade foods company serving growing global healthy and sustainable foods markets, with the goal of creating long-term value for our operating partners, customers, team members and shareholders. We continue to gain momentum in our business and believe our third quarter results reflect another important point in our journey. At the same time, we are working to expand our geographic footprint and product mix with the goal of increasing our market presence and operating margins through increased value-add."

Fiscal 2026 Third Quarter Results Overview

  • Third quarter 2026 sales of $25.2 million versus $15.1 million in the prior year, an increase of approximately 67%. Sales increased as new business was on-boarded and existing customers increased their sales versus the prior year. Sales for the third quarter of 2026 are the largest third quarter sales in the Company's history.
  • Gross profit of $1.5 million or 5.8% of sales, versus $1.2 million or 8.2% of sales in the prior year, an increase of approximately 18% in gross profit dollars. Adjusted gross profit (1) of $2.1 million or 8.2% of sales when accounting for the impact of realized gains on derivatives related to gross profit versus $0.7 million or 4.5% of sales in the prior year, an increase of approximately 206%. Gross profit and adjusted gross profit (1) dollars for the third quarter of 2026 are the largest third quarter gross profit dollars in the history of the Company.
  • Cash overhead expenses (1) of $2.0 million or7.8% of sales versus $1.3 million or 8.9% of sales in the prior year. Cash overhead expenses (1) as a percentage of sales improved versus the prior periods as the business continues to grow and scale and overheads are leveraged on an expanded platform. Costs increased with the addition of administrative and logistics resources required to support significant growth in the business and include $0.2 million related to future oriented corporate development costs.
  • Income from operations (1) excluding stock-based compensation and including realized gains/losses on derivatives related to gross profit of $0.0 million versus a loss of $0.7 million in the prior year.
  • Net interest and accretion costs of $0.1 million versus $0.1 million in the prior year, reflecting lower costs as debt was repaid or restructured in the first half of 2025, resulting in no long-term debt being outstanding as of September 30, 2026.
  • Realized gain of $0.6 million on derivatives versus a loss of $0.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. Unrealized loss on derivative assets of $0.5 million versus an unrealized gain of $1.0 million in the prior year. Derivative assets represent hedges on foreign currencies which are intended to protect the Company's gross profit.
  • Net loss for the third quarter of $1.4 million versus a net loss of $2.0 million in the third quarter of the prior year. Prior year results include a loss on the settlement of debt of $1.7 million and restructuring costs of $0.1 million related to the restructuring of the balance sheet which occurred in 2025.

Fiscal 2026 Nine-Month Results Overview

  • Sales of $78.5 million versus $45.9 million in the prior year, an increase of approximately 71%. Sales increased throughout the first three quarters as new business was on-boarded and existing customers increased their sales versus the prior year.
  • Gross profit of $5.3 million or 6.8% of sales, versus $3.6 million or 7.9% of sales in the prior year, an increase of approximately 48% in gross profit dollars. Adjusted gross profit (1) dollars of $5.9 million or 7.5% of sales when accounting for the impact of realized gains/ losses on derivatives related to gross profit versus $2.5 million or 5.5% of sales in the prior year, an increase of approximately 134%.
  • Cash overhead expenses (1) of $5.3 million or 6.8% of sales versus $3.4 million or 7.4% of sales in the prior year. Cash overhead expenses (1) as a percentage of sales improved versus the prior period as the business continues to grow and scale and overheads are leveraged on an expanded platform. Costs include $0.2 million related to future oriented corporate development expenses.
  • Income from operations (1) excluding stock-based compensation and including realized gains/losses on derivatives related to gross profit of $0.3 million versus a loss of $1.0 million in the prior year.
  • Net interest and accretion costs of $0.2 million versus $0.6 million in the prior year, reflecting lower borrowing costs as debt was repaid or restructured in the first half of 2025, resulting in no long-term debt being outstanding as of September 30, 2026.
  • Realized gain on derivatives of $0.5 million versus a loss of $1.1 million in the prior year. Unrealized gain on derivative assets of $1.0 million versus an unrealized loss of $1.2 million in the prior year. Derivative assets represent hedges on foreign currencies which are intended to protect the Company's gross profit.
  • Net loss of $1.7 million versus a loss of $9.6 million in the prior year. Prior year results include a loss on the settlement of debt of $5.5 million and restructuring costs of $0.8 million, related to the restructuring of the balance sheet which occurred in 2025.

Investor Conference Call

The Company will host a conference call for investors and analysts to discuss its third quarter 2026 financial results on December 1, 2026, at 12:00 pm EST. Organto Food's CEO and Co-Chair, Steve Bromley and President, Darryl Bergman, will provide a corporate update, review the financial results, and discuss the Company's outlook, followed by a Q&A session.

Details on how to attend are detailed below:

  • Registration link: https://organto.com/organto-q3-webinar-2026-11-nr/
  • Date: December 1, 2026
  • Time: 12:00 pm EST

The Company's filings including unaudited Financial Statements and accompanying Management's Discussion and Analysis for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and Audited Financial Statements and accompanying Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2025, can be found at www.SEDARplus.ca or at the Company's website at www.organto.com under the Investors tab.

(1) The information presented herein refers to the non-IFRS financial measures of adjusted gross profit, cash overhead expenses, income from operations and adjusted EBITDA. (i) Adjusted gross profit - we hedge currencies for certain product categories where either the supply or sales commitments are fixed in foreign currencies. The realized gains and losses from these hedging activities are combined with gross profit to determine adjusted gross profit. (ii) Cash overhead expenses - refers to the combination of selling, general and administration expenses, management fees and labour costs and benefits less non-cash costs included in these expense categories. (iii) Income from operations - refers to the net result of the net loss for the period excluding non-cash stock-based compensation, interest expense and accretion, other income, unrealized gains/losses on derivative assets and liabilities, restructuring costs, gain (loss) on the settlement of debt and foreign exchange gains (losses). (iv) Adjusted EBITDA - refers to income from operations adjusted for depreciation and amortization and certain future-oriented costs. These measures are not recognized measures under IFRS and do not have a standardized meaning prescribed by IFRS. Non-IFRS financial measures should not be considered in isolation nor as a substitute for analysis of the Company's financial information reported under IFRS and are unlikely to be comparable to similar measures presented by other issuers. Rather, these measures are provided as additional information to complement those IFRS measures by providing further understanding of the Company's results from management's perspective and thus highlight trends in its business that may not otherwise be apparent when relying solely on IFRS measures. The Company believes that securities analysts, investors and other interested parties frequently use non-IFRS financial measures in the evaluation of the Company. The Company's management also uses non-IFRS financial measures to facilitate operating performance comparisons from period to period and to prepare annual operating budgets and forecasts.

(2) Annualized sales run rate is calculated by adjusting the YTD sales by multiplying the YTD sales by 365 days and dividing that number by the number of days in the YTD period.

CALGARY, AB / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / Jade Leader Corp, ("Jade Leader" or the "Company") announces a change of the Company's auditor. At the request of the Company, BDO Canada LLP (the "Former Auditor") has resigned as auditor of the Company effective November 26, 2026. The audit committee and board of directors of the Company have appointed Crowe MacKay LLP as the successor auditor, effective November 26, 2026 (the "Successor Auditor") and this appointment will be placed before Shareholders for approval thereto at the Corporation's next Annual General Meeting.

The Company has sent a Notice of Change of Auditor (the "Notice") to the Former Auditor and to the Successor Auditor and has received a letter from each, addressed to the securities commissions in each of Alberta, British Columbia and Ontario stating that they agree with the information contained in the Notice. The Notice together with the letter from the Former Auditor and the letter from the Successor Auditor have been reviewed and approved by the Company's board of directors and are available on the SEDAR+ website at www.sedarplus.ca.

There were no disagreements or unresolved issues between the Company and the Former Auditor on any matter of audit scope or procedures, accounting principles or policies, or financial statement disclosure. It is the Company's opinion that there have been no "reportable events" (as defined in National Instrument 51-102 - Continuous Disclosure Obligations) between the Company and the Former Auditor. The Former Auditor did not provide a modified opinion in their auditor's report for the financial statements of the Company for the fiscal years ended September 30, 2024 and September 30, 2025.

data.title: North American Launch - Prevost Unveils Its First-Ever Fully Electric Motorcoach
data.description:
North American Launch - Prevost Unveils Its First-Ever Fully Electric Motorcoach

North American Launch - Prevost Unveils Its First-Ever Fully Electric Motorcoach

PR Newswire

SAINTE-CLAIRE, QC, Nov. 26, 2026

SAINTE-CLAIRE, QC, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Prevost, North America's largest motorcoach manufacturer, is proud to announce the North American launch of its first zero-emission motorcoach, the H3-45 Electric.

"The development of our new fully electric motorcoach demonstrates Prevost's commitment to innovation and to bringing zero-emission powertrains to the market. By pursuing this ambition, we are helping build more sustainable mobility while developing advanced expertise and innovative jobs at Prevost. This milestone reflects our determination to combine technological progress with the needs expressed by some of our customers," said François Tremblay, President of Prevost and Volvo Group Canada.

The Prevost H3-45 Electric combines the premium H-Series experience with a fully integrated Volvo electric propulsion system engineered for demanding motorcoach applications. Its dual-motor electric drivetrain delivers 450 kW of rated power, paired with an automated 8-speed transmission and regenerative braking to recover energy during deceleration.

Six Volvo Cube 2 lithium-ion battery packs provide 459 kWh of usable energy, supported by an advanced liquid-based thermal management system designed to maintain optimal battery performance across varying operating conditions. With CCS1 and MCS charging compatibility and charging capability up to 350 kW (CCS1), the H3-45 Electric brings together performance, efficiency and operational flexibility while preserving the familiar driver environment, ride quality and premium experience that define a Prevost coach.

"Transportation electrification is part of the long-term evolution of our industry in North America. Today, with this new vehicle, we are doing what Prevost has always done best: listening to our customers, anticipating their needs and innovating to offer transportation solutions tailored to their needs," concluded Tremblay.

About PREVOST

Prevost has provided coach solutions for a century with an uncompromising commitment to quality, a drive for constant innovation and improvement, and dedication to safety and sustainability in every business aspect. Today, Prevost is one of North America's largest producers of premium intercity touring coaches and is the world leader in the production of high-end motorhome and specialty conversion coaches. Customer support is secured via the largest service network in the motorcoach industry with strategically located OEM-owned and operated service centers across North America, a specialized customer support team with more than 260 years of industry experience, and 50+ mobile service vans. Prevost manufacturing facilities are located in Sainte-Claire, Quebec, Canada.

Prevost is part of the Volvo Group, one of the world's leading manufacturers of buses, trucks, construction equipment, power solutions for marine and industrial applications, financing and services that increase customer uptime and productivity. For more information, please visit www.volvogroup.com.
